text:
jess (Support): hey team — escalation from ACME Foods. Their integration to our streaming (SSE) endpoint keeps dropping mid-response when their downstream consumer is slow. They see partial JSON blobs and client reconnects that cause duplicate items. Customer says this is affecting billing and UX.

alex (Customer): throwing logs here — we open /v1/stream?model=red-q & then after ~15s we get a chunk, then socket closes. reconnect returns the rest but duplicates some token ranges. sometimes we get 'write error: EAGAIN' in the client. no proxy in front of us, direct to our node.

jess (Support): thanks, alex. Do you have a minimal repro we can run? Also any auth or quota noise?

alex (Customer): no auth failures — token stays valid. quotas fine. I can repro with curl: 
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=small"
```
If I throttle the consumer (sleep in a line processor), after some writes the connection just closes. client gets ECONNRESET and then reconnects automatically.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1435 (severity: high) — assigned to eng-sre.

sanjay (Eng-SRE): pinging runtime team. Maya, any recent changes to the streaming path or socket buffer handling?

maya (Eng-Runtime): nothing intentional rolled last week. We did a kernel param bump on some hosts (tcp_mem) but only for a subset. Need logs from the server side — grep for "write"/"EAGAIN"/"backpressure" around the timestamp.

jess (Support): alex — can you share full client logs (including errno) and exact timestamps? We want to correlate with gateway and node logs. Also, does the app use HTTP/1.1 chunked SSE or HTTP/2?

alex (Customer): HTTP/1.1 SSE. log excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:21:18Z] write 4096 -> 0 bytes written, errno=11 (EAGAIN)
[2026-03-12T14:21:18Z] write 4096 -> 0 bytes written, errno=11 (EAGAIN)
[2026-03-12T14:21:18Z] connection reset by peer
```
Then client reconnects and server stream resumes at message id 42 but we get again message id 40-44 duplicates.

sanjay (Eng-SRE): that pattern looks like slow-consumer backpressure where the socket send buffer is full, kernel returns EAGAIN, our runtime currently retries a few times then aborts the connection to avoid resource starvation. We should confirm our retry policy and socket options (TCP_NODELAY, send buffer sizes).

maya (Eng-Runtime): confirming: runtime currently does 3 retry attempts with a 50ms backoff on EAGAIN before aborting the request. We set SO_SNDBUF to 64KB by default and rely on the OS. For very slow consumers that don't read for tens of seconds, the buffer fills and we abort to protect the worker.

jess (Support): customer is upset because reconnects cause duplicates and they get billed for both attempts. Alex — do you get duplicate billing events or double-counted tokens?

alex (Customer): tokens billed twice sometimes. Our backend counts each successful chunk. When reconnect resumes, we get the remainder and our systems think it's a new stream. Billing dashboard shows two short streams.

sanjay (Eng-SRE): billing team — we might need to credit duplicates if caused by server abort. But we should first find a mitigation to avoid aborts. Ideas: a) longer retry/backoff on EAGAIN for SSE endpoints b) explicit Flow-Control via headers or chunk ACKs c) graceful pause/resume with resume token so duplicates are avoided d) server-side buffering limit docs and SDK guidance to customers.

maya (Eng-Runtime): agree. Short term we can: increase retry attempts from 3 -> 10 with exponential backoff up to 1s, and add a metric for "sse_write_retries" and tag by customer. Long term: add a small resumable protocol that emits explicit message IDs and resume tokens (but that is non-trivial for hosted API).

jess (Support): alex — would increasing server retries help your use case? If the server waits longer, you would eventually drain and avoid a reset. Any constraints on client (they don't want huge latencies).

alex (Customer): they can't pause forever — they want low-ish latency, but they can handle an extra 1s. Duplicate billing is the bigger problem. If you bump retries to say 1s total, that should cut most aborts. Also can we expose a resume token header so client can dedupe on reconnect?

maya (Eng-Runtime): notes: we can land a config change to extend retries for SSE endpoints only and add a "X-Redwood-Resume-Id: <id>" header emitted periodically so clients can detect overlap. That would be a small instrumented change.

sanjay (Eng-SRE): also add runbook entries: tune SO_SNDBUF on hosts serving high SSE traffic, and watch the new metric. If we see a large number of EAGAIN+abort for a specific customer, auto-create an internal ticket.

jess (Support): billing follow-up — we need to check if duplicates in billing are from double successful responses or from client-side replay. @billing-team can you freeze credits for ACME Foods until we confirm?

ops-bot: billing notification sent to billing-team channel.

maya (Eng-Runtime): repro steps I used locally in a container to simulate a slow consumer: 
```bash
# server: run local dev runtime on 8080 (SSE endpoint)
# client: use netcat and sleep between reads
printf 'GET /v1/stream?model=mini HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nAuthorization: Bearer $KEY\r\n\r\n' | nc localhost 8080 > /tmp/out &
# then chunk-read with artificial slowness
python3 -c "import sys, time; f=open('/tmp/out');
 while True:
  c=f.read(1)
  if not c: break
  sys.stdout.write(c); sys.stdout.flush(); time.sleep(0.2)"
```
This reproduces buffered socket, repeated EAGAIN in server, then abort after retries.

jess (Support): perfect — can you drop the exact runtime logs when EAGAIN -> abort happens so we can attach to the ticket?

maya (Eng-Runtime): attached: log snippet. We added a clearer message: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:21:18Z] sse: write attempt 1 failed errno=11
[2026-03-12T14:21:18Z] sse: write attempt 2 failed errno=11
[2026-03-12T14:21:18Z] sse: write attempt 3 failed errno=11
[2026-03-12T14:21:18Z] sse: write abort after retries -> closing connection customer=ACME id=abc123
```

sanjay (Eng-SRE): action items: 
- maya: roll config patch to increase SSE EAGAIN retries (canary 10% hosts) and add metric (sse.write.retries).
- maya: emit periodic X-Redwood-Resume-Id header for SSE endpoints.
- billing: hold credits / investigate duplicates for ACME.
- support: coordinate with customer and advise temporary client-side mitigation (reduce per-line processing, add dedupe on message id).

jess (Support): noted. Alex — temporary client suggestions: 1) implement idempotency/dedupe by message id, 2) add jittered backoff on reconnect to avoid multiple simultaneous handoffs, 3) set TCP keepalive so idle network doesn't drop. We'll follow up with timeline for the server change.

alex (Customer): ok thanks. we can add dedupe on our side but would appreciate credits. Keep me posted.

maya (Eng-Runtime): will post a canary rollout timeline here once merged (~3h for canary + monitoring).

sanjay (Eng-SRE): adding a dashboard panel for sse.write.retries and EAGAIN abort rate. If the canary shows reduction in aborts we expand rollout.

jess (Support): closing loop: logged internal ticket RED-STREAM-872. Will update customer after canary result. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: INC-2026-1435 transitioned to status: in_progress
